purpose: Metadata-only receipt for the PRIVATE candidate capture. The raw candidate snapshots stay OUTSIDE Git and outside every shareable diagnostics export.

captureImplementation.seam: the compaction DECISION boundary, AFTER the decision arithmetic and BEFORE any compaction work

separateExplicitOptIn.separation: SEPARATE from the shareable latency/trace opt-in — enabling the metadata trace does NOT arm the private capture. The opt-in is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT: the closed-runtime dogfood identity is also required.
notArmedValues: the opt-in alone (without the dogfood identity)

isolatedDogfoodRuntimeOnly.matching: EXACT, fail-closed (an absent, empty, whitespace, differently-cased, or otherwise-valued marker resolves to 'public')
isolatedDogfoodRuntimeOnly.rationale: Reuses the established closed-runtime dogfood identity (apps/vscode/src/sdk/dogfood-runtime-profile.ts) rather than inventing a second profile bit.
witnesses: core/compaction-candidate-capture.test.ts :: 'the private capture is armed ONLY by an explicit separate opt-in AND the dogfood identity'
core/compaction-candidate-capture.test.ts :: 'P0-3: a REGULAR profile can NEVER arm the capture, even with the opt-in set'

privateDirectory.fallback: NONE — there is no implicit ~/.cline/data fallback; with no explicit storage root the capture is NOT armed at all (fail closed)
privateDirectory.witness: core/compaction-candidate-capture.test.ts :: 'P0-3: the storage root FAILS CLOSED — there is no implicit ~/.cline/data fallback'

permissions.existingEntriesCorrected: chmod is applied explicitly to the directory and to every file the store writes, because mkdir/writeFile `mode` only applies to NEWLY created entries
witnesses: core/compaction-candidate-capture.test.ts :: 'the private directory uses restrictive POSIX permissions'
core/compaction-candidate-capture.test.ts :: 'P0-3: a PERMISSIVE pre-existing directory and file are CORRECTED, not inherited'

bounds.maxCandidatesScope: The cap counts the CONTROL and the COMPACTION candidates TOGETHER. A control does NOT get a slot on top of the cap: the directory never holds more than 12 candidate files, whatever the mix.
bounds.enforcement: ON THE WRITE — an oversized candidate is REJECTED BEFORE ANY BYTE IS WRITTEN and reported as a metadata-only rejection receipt; the oversized content never lands on disk
bounds.diskAccounting: The store tracks the files it owns and derives the byte/count totals from that map, so the reported totals are the ACTUAL on-disk totals
witnesses: core/compaction-candidate-capture.test.ts :: 'P0-1: an oversized candidate is REJECTED BEFORE the write — the disk stays bounded'
core/compaction-candidate-capture.test.ts :: 'P0-1: repeated captures keep the ACTUAL disk file count and byte total bounded'
core/compaction-candidate-capture.test.ts :: 'P0-1: a SUPERSEDED control candidate is REMOVED from disk'
core/compaction-candidate-capture.identity-retention.test.ts :: 'I2: the hard retention cap counts the CONTROL and the compaction candidates TOGETHER'
core/compaction-candidate-capture.identity-retention.test.ts :: 'I2: the 12 → 13 → 14 candidate transitions NEVER exceed the declared maximum on disk'
core/compaction-candidate-capture.identity-retention.test.ts :: 'I3: the reported count and byte totals RECONCILE with the actual directory'

storageIdentity.rule: A capture file is identified by the DECISION's storage identity ALONGSIDE the content fingerprint: `<storage identity>--<content fingerprint>.json`.
storageIdentity.storageIdentitySource: the candidate's decisionId, else its preparationRequestId; a candidate carrying NEITHER gets a monotonic ordinal so it still receives its own file
storageIdentity.identityResolvedAt: record() — the file name is stable for the candidate's whole lifetime across every subsequent flush
storageIdentity.whyNotContentFingerprintAlone: The content fingerprint identifies WHAT was measured, not WHICH decision measured it. Two distinct eligibility decisions can measure byte-identical content; naming both files after the content collapsed them onto one file and the second write silently OVERWROTE the first decision's snapshot.
witnesses: core/compaction-candidate-capture.identity-retention.test.ts :: 'I1: DISTINCT decisions with IDENTICAL content do NOT collapse onto one file'

writeSafety.serializationMechanism: a per-store promise chain: an overlapping flush starts only after the previous one completes. Node explicitly warns against overlapping writeFile() calls to the same file — the writes can interleave and leave a corrupt file behind.
writeSafety.chainDoesNotBreakOnFailure: a rejected flush does not poison subsequent flushes
writeSafety.idempotenceRationale: A candidate whose serialized bytes are unchanged is not rewritten, so a previously persisted snapshot is not needlessly re-exposed and the directory is not churned on every flush.
witnesses: core/compaction-candidate-capture.identity-retention.test.ts :: 'I4: overlapping flushes are serialized and never corrupt a captured file'
core/compaction-candidate-capture.identity-retention.test.ts :: 'I4b: an unchanged payload is NOT rewritten on a subsequent flush'

retention.evictionOrder: the OLDEST compaction candidate is evicted first; the control is evicted only when nothing older remains to drop

explicitRemoval.witness: core/compaction-candidate-capture.test.ts :: 'the capture retains ONE control ... and is removable'

appliedAt: the write boundary (capture store) — defence in depth

failureIsolation.behaviour: a capture failure is swallowed and never changes the runtime's behaviour

immutableSnapshot.behaviour: record() deep-copies and freezes the candidate BEFORE the first asynchronous boundary, so a later mutation of the live request objects cannot change what the 'exact' snapshot represents
immutableSnapshot.witness: core/compaction-candidate-capture.test.ts :: 'P1: the captured snapshot is IMMUTABLE — a later mutation cannot change it'

snapshotSchema.estimatedInputTokens: <the production estimator's requestInputTokens at the decision>
snapshotSchema.requestTriggerTokens: <the production resolver's requestTriggerTokens at the decision>

liveCaptureNote: The capture is implemented, privacy-witnessed and armed-by-opt-in. No live snapshot was produced by this run because the exact-head dogfood VSIX is built manually by the operator. The schema above is the CONTRACT, not a measured observation.

exactCountingEligibility.rule: a snapshot is eligible for exact counting only when snapshotComplete === true AND truncated === false

contentsRecordedHere: NONE — this receipt carries only references, hashes and classifications. The raw candidate bodies remain in the private directory and are never committed.
